title: Spreading a generic-fibre partial isomorphism to a common open
statement:
Let X,Y,S be affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with S integral
[def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let f:X\to S and g:Y\to S be locally finitely presented
[def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let \eta be a generic point of S. Assume
X_\eta [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is nonempty. Let p be a partial isomorphism from X_\eta
to Y_\eta: p consists of dense open subschemes U\subset X_\eta and U'\subset Y_\eta
and an isomorphism U\to U'. Assume it commutes with the structure maps to
\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta). Then there exist an open V\subset X and an open immersion
i:V\to Y [def-weil-open-immersion] such that i followed by g equals f restricted to V,
and \eta lies in the image of V\to S. No reducedness, irreducibility, flatness, or
special-fibre density is asserted for the original families.

source.place: Tag 0559, lemma-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibre, first proof, common-open paragraph; Tag 0552, function-field criterion for birationality of integral schemes locally of finite type; Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, morphism descent and eventual equality

proof.text: Density and nonemptiness give a point in the source of p. Choose an affine neighbourhood A of that point within p.source. Its image U in X_eta is affine, and its image T under p.iso followed by the target inclusion is affine, since these maps are open immersions. The canonical image isomorphisms give e:U -> T over Spec kappa(eta). This uses only one affine neighbourhood; no intersection of independently chosen source and target charts is needed.

Apply exists_affine_open_lift_of_generic_fibre to U and T, obtaining affine opens V in X and W in Y and generic-fibre isomorphisms a and b with their structure-map equations. Transport e to a generic-fibre isomorphism between V and W; the displayed equations prove it is over kappa(eta).

Apply exists_base_open_iso_of_generic_fibre_iso to V and W. Their inclusions are locally finitely presented open immersions, so their composites with f and g remain locally finitely presented. This produces a base neighbourhood B of eta and an isomorphism c between the restrictions of V and W to B over S.

Let Z be the preimage of B in V and O its image in X. Compose the inverse canonical image isomorphism O -> Z with c and the two target open inclusions. This is an open immersion i:O -> Y, and c's projection equation proves i is over S. Transport the original chosen point of U by a^{-1} to the generic fibre of V. Its fibre-inclusion image v maps to eta, so v lies in Z because eta lies in B. Its image in O witnesses eta in the range of O -> S.

proof_origin.note: T4: one affine chart in the partial-isomorphism source, its affine image, affine-open lifting through the generic-point limit, and whole-isomorphism descent. All helper theorems proved without sorry.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_of_generic_fibre_partial_iso
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] [IsAffine S] [IsIntegral S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g]
    (η : S) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) [Nonempty (f.fiber η)]
    (p : (f.fiber η).PartialIso (g.fiber η))
    (hp : p.IsOver (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η) (g.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ V : X.Opens, η ∈ Set.range (V.ι ≫ f) ∧
      ∃ i : V.toScheme ⟶ Y, IsOpenImmersion i ∧ i ≫ g = V.ι ≫ f
